sources.entry: Oh My Git!: a game to learn git

summary.title: Oh My Git!
summary.one_liner: An open source game that teaches Git by visualizing repository internals in real time, with playing cards, an integrated Git terminal, and remote-collaboration workflows.
takeaways: Oh My Git! shows how Git repository structures change in real time as you act on them.
Playing cards pair each Git command with a short description and an icon, serving as both action and documentation.
An integrated terminal runs a real Git, so advanced players can try any Git command.
The game focuses on remotes and multi-repository workflows for team collaboration.
Binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows via itch.io; the project is open source and discussed on GitHub.
summary.summary: Oh My Git! is an open source game for learning Git, described on its homepage as a way to see how Git repositories' internal structures change in real time as the player acts. It uses a playing-card interface to introduce commands with descriptions and icons, and an integrated terminal running real Git for experimentation. The game also covers remotes and collaboration workflows across multiple repositories. The page links to binaries on itch.io, GitHub for issues and the README, and the project's press kit and talks.
